metalboi.gui.option.renderer_enabled.too: Renders the frame at a lower internal resolution and resamples it back up to your display, which is the single biggest frame-rate lever available on macOS. The tooltip below also reports the graphics backend actually in use.
metalboi.gui.option.log_backend.tooltip: Writes a one-line report of the detected GL vendor, renderer and version to latest.log on the first rendered frame.
metalboi.gui.option.render_scale.tooltip: Internal render resolution as a percentage of your window. Lower values shade far fewer pixels and give a large frame-rate increase; on a Retina display the default framebuffer is already 2x in each axis, so the gains are bigger than they look. 100% is native resolution. The HUD scales with this setting so the interface stays laid out correctly.
metalboi.gui.option.upscaler.tooltip.nea: Hard pixel replication. Cheapest option, no blur, but visibly blocky below about 85%.
metalboi.gui.option.upscaler.tooltip.bil: Linear interpolation - what Minecraft itself uses when sizes differ. Cheapest smooth option and the familiar baseline.
metalboi.gui.option.upscaler.tooltip.bic: Catmull-Rom bicubic, 16 taps. Clearly sharper than bilinear with no ringing. Recommended default.
metalboi.gui.option.upscaler.tooltip.lan: Lanczos-2, 16 taps. The sharpest pure resampler here; adds slight ringing on very high-contrast edges such as block outlines and text.
metalboi.gui.option.upscaler.tooltip.sha: Bicubic with a deepened negative lobe, driven by the sharpening slider. Same cost as bicubic, and the best choice at low render scales where softness is the main complaint.
metalboi.gui.option.sharpness.tooltip: How far the bicubic kernel's negative lobe is pushed beyond neutral Catmull-Rom. 0% is identical to the Bicubic upscaler; 100% is the strongest edge emphasis. Only used when the upscaler is set to Sharpened bicubic.
